 Advertisement Election Day: Tracking the weather as midterm voters head to polls
 Here are all the maps you need before you head to the polls.
 By Rob Shackelford • just now Updated: November 3, 2026, 9:16 am EST Published: November 3, 2026, 9:07 am EST Share Share
 1 . East forecast Chevron Down Voters arrive to cast their ballots on Election Day at Johnson County Arts & Heritage Center on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026, in Overland Park, Kansas.
 ( Jim Vondruska/Getty Images )
 Millions are heading to the polls for Election Day, and in some areas, voters will need to dodge less-than-ideal weather conditions. 
 A storm system will bring showers and thunderstorms to the central U.S., including Chicago, Minneapolis, Kansas City and Houston.
 And in Florida, prolonged flooding forced state officials to move 19 polling locations in Brevard, Highlands, Indian River, Martin, Okeechobee, Palm Beach and St. Lucie counties, according to CNN.com. Parts of Florida have received more than a foot of rain in recent days, prompting Gov. Ron DeSantis to declare a state of emergency.

 Polls are open in most states from early in the morning through the early evening. You can find more state-by-state information on where to vote here .
 All 435 members of the U.S. House of Representatives are up for election Tuesday. There are also U.S. Senate races in 35 states.
